synopsis: UNECE NATM credibility assessment is identified as a main simulation credibility reference alongside SET Level, IAMTS and several ASAM initiatives; that reference set is characterized as on-road and pre-standard [f8323]. The NATM framework is dated 2022–2024 and, alongside NASA-STD-7009B and ASME V&V 40, ties simulation credibility to a defined use and the consequence of error [f9454]. The planning requirement makes this explicit: credibility must be stated relative to intended use, operating envelope and consequence of error [f10293]. NATM's evidence is explicitly on-road, so these facts do not establish its applicability to heavy off-road machines [f8323, f9454, f10293].

relations.note: The planning requirement adds the operating envelope to the shared use-and-error-consequence position.
Use-specific credibility principles explain NATM's inclusion among main simulation credibility references.
Adds NATM's dates and credibility principles to the reference inventory.
